important.name: B10 is green on a baseline that never ran the skill
important.summary:
B10's only baseline, R-9, is a session that never loaded the round-1 spec-it skill: it 'went straight to the plan with no design sheet' and wrote ActionPlan 2032 into the tree. Its judged item (a goal line holding two outcomes) was graded absent against an expected present, so the behavior itself never went red; the only red signal is the SC-9 reply_matches 'next: /harness:write-plan' check, which any session without the skill fails by construction. That proves the skill exists, not that it splits compound asks. B11, B12 and B13 were dropped in round 3 for exactly this outcome (baseline did not fail), so the spec now applies two standards to the same evidence. The release note even admits the B10 baseline 'waits on a baseline run from a session that loads this plugin version'.

Also (docs): B10 ('one goal line per outcome' when no fork is open) passed its baseline gate only through the SC-9 `reply_matches next: /harness:write-plan` check (SkillSpec.json:442-448, R-9 detail 'observed False'). Without the skill no session prints that line, so this check fails for every baseline whatever the reply does. The judged item, the compound goal line the rule targets, graded 'absent' in baseline R-9 (lines 1116-1120: 'I went straight to the plan with no design sheet first'). So the baseline never showed the line-splitting failure B10 claims to fix, and the release note credits the round with proving that behavior.
fix: Reopen, rerun the B10 baseline from a session that loads the round-1 skill (claude --plugin-dir plugins/harness at the round-1 tree), regrade, and keep B10 only if the judged item goes red; otherwise drop it with a dropped_reason like B11-B13.
If the strap gate is meant to accept a check-only red, state that in B10's rationale and in docs/RELEASES/v1.1.0.md so the evidence is not read as a behavioral baseline.

In a later round, give B10 a scenario whose baseline writes goal lines (for example one where the task itself asks for a written goals list), so the judged compound-line item can be 'present' at baseline.
Or state in the release entry that B10's red came from the hand-off check alone.

important.name: A request holding 'Date: ' or '## ' at a wrapped line start renders a page parse_sheet refuses
important.summary:
The spec_it_api module docstring (spec_it_api.py:3-4) and SkillSpec B2 claim that parse_sheet reverses render_sheet. render_sheet (spec_it_models.py:110-111) wraps the request as plain lines under '## Request'. parse_sheet (spec_it_models.py:148-151) then scans every line for DATE_PREFIX and every line for '## ' headings. Example: the request 'Date: shown in the banner.' passes every SpecSheet validator, and write_sheet writes it. load_sheet and 'spec_it.py check' then refuse the page: two 'Date: ' lines give 'the page needs one Date: YYYY-MM-DD line'. A request word that wraps to the start of a line as '## Goals' fails the same way. The SKILL's loop is 'fix the field it names and rerun; never edit the page by hand' (SKILL.md:67,89), but this problem line names no field, so the loop dead-ends on a sheet the API itself wrote.

Also (roast): render_sheet wraps the request at 110 columns, and parse_sheet treats any line starting with 'Date: ' as the date line and any line starting with '## ' as a heading. A request whose wrap lands 'Date: ...' or '## Goals' at a line start passes SpecSheet validation and write_sheet writes it, then load_sheet and `spec_it.py check` refuse the page ('the page needs one Date: YYYY-MM-DD line'). Reproduced: request = 'word ' * 22 + 'Date: tomorrow is fine.' round-trips to a ValueError. The module docstring promises render_sheet writes and parse_sheet reads back the only stored form; here the API writes a sheet the skill then forbids editing by hand. Rare, but the kind of rare that ruins a Friday.

Also (adv_code_runtime): render_sheet wraps the request with textwrap at 110 columns and writes the lines bare; parse_sheet treats any line starting with '## ' as a section heading and any line starting with 'Date: ' as the date line. The request validator only bans ids/URLs/fences, so a request that begins with (or wraps onto a line beginning with) '## <word>' or 'Date: ' validates, writes, and then fails to parse: an unknown or duplicate section, or two Date lines.

Also (runtime): render_sheet wraps the request with textwrap at 110 columns, so any word of the request can start a page line. parse_sheet then takes every line starting with 'Date: ' as a date line (spec_it_models.py:148-150) and every line starting with '## ' as a section heading (_sections, 123-127). A request such as '<~105 chars> Date: field shown on the form' renders a second 'Date: ' line, and one holding '## Goals' renders a stray heading: write_sheet accepts and writes the page, then spec_it.py check (and load_sheet) refuses it. That breaks the contract the SKILL.md step 3 states (write_sheet 'renders the only layout check accepts') and the agent is told never to edit the page by hand, leaving no way forward but rewording the request blindly. The same split happens for a title, goal or avoid line holding '\r' in the title or any str.splitlines separator other than '\n'/'\r' ('\x0c', '\x1c', '\u2028', ...): _title checks only '\n' (79-82) and _statement only '\n'/'\r' (56-57), while parse_sheet splits on all of them (143).

Also (overall): The model accepts sheets whose rendered page fails its own parser, so the skill's write step succeeds and its check step then refuses a page the developer was told never to hand-edit. Two routes: (1) `_title` (lines 77-82) rejects only '\n' and `_statement` (lines 56-57) only '\n'/'\r', but `parse_sheet` splits with `str.splitlines()`, which also breaks on '\r' (title), '\v', '\f', '\x1c'-'\x1e', '\x85', '\u2028' and '\u2029'; such a title or goal renders across two lines and the round-trip check at line 157 fails. (2) `render_sheet` wraps the request at 110 columns (line 111), so a request that mentions 'Date: ...' or '## Goals' can land that text at the start of a wrapped line; `parse_sheet` then counts two 'Date: ' lines (lines 148-150) or raises 'unexpected section' from `_sections` (line 125). The refusal names the page layout, not the field, so the SKILL.md loop 'fix the field it names and rerun' has nothing to act on.

Attack: Probe (run at PR head): SpecSheet(title='T', request='## Goals first then more', goals=['g'], day=date(2026,11,25)) constructs; parse_sheet(render_sheet(s)) raises "unexpected section '## Goals first then more'". request='Date: 2026-01-01 is the cutoff' raises "the page needs one 'Date: YYYY-MM-DD' line". Mid-text also breaks: request=('x ' * 54) + 'Date: 2026-01-01 later' wraps so a line starts with 'Date: ' and parse fails the same way. write_sheet accepts all three, then `spec_it.py check` on the written file exits 1.
fix: In parse_sheet, read the date only from lines[2], refuse when lines[2] does not start with DATE_PREFIX, and treat a '## ' line as a heading only when it matches the exact '## Request'/'## Goals'/'## Avoid' sequence render_sheet emits. Add a test that round-trips the request 'Date: shown in the banner.'.
In SpecSheet._whole, refuse a sheet whose wrapped request lines start with DATE_PREFIX or '## ', naming the request in the message, so write_sheet refuses what check would refuse.

In parse_sheet, read the date only from lines[2] and accept '## ' headings only at the positions render_sheet emits (or split the body on the exact '

## Goals

' / '

## Avoid

' separators), so request text cannot impersonate structure; add a test with a request that wraps 'Date: ' and '## Avoid' to a line start.
Refuse 'Date: ' and '## ' inside the request in SpecSheet._request, with a problem message naming the field, and add the same test.
Refuse such a request in SpecSheet (e.g. in _whole, check that no rendered request line starts with '## ' or DATE_PREFIX, or that '## '/'Date: ' tokens do not appear in the request).
Make parse_sheet positional: take the date only from line 3 and recognize headings only at the known positions, so request text can never be read as structure.

Read the date only from its fixed slot (lines[2]) in parse_sheet, and have _sections stop treating '## ' lines as headings inside the Request body (or refuse, in the _request validator, a request whose wrapped lines start with '## ' or DATE_PREFIX); refuse in _title and _statement any text where len(text.splitlines()) > 1.

In SpecSheet._whole, after rendering, check that the rendered page has exactly one DATE_PREFIX line and exactly the expected '## ' headings, and that the title and each item occupy one line, raising ValueError otherwise so write_sheet refuses what check would refuse.

Make the one-line checks match the parser: in `_statement` and `_title` refuse when `len(text.splitlines()) != 1` instead of testing only '\n'/'\r'; and in `_whole`, after rendering, refuse (naming the request) when any wrapped request line starts with '## ' or with `DATE_PREFIX`.

In `_whole`, run the structural half of `parse_sheet` (the `DATE_PREFIX` count and `_sections`) on the rendered page without constructing a new SpecSheet, so any page the model accepts is one the parser accepts; add a model test for each route.

important.name: spec-it hand-off drops the TODO ids and issues that write-plan now expects in --refs
important.summary: write-plan step 1 (plugins/harness/skills/write-plan/SKILL.md:37-39) now says a sheet carries no ids, so the TODO ids and issues the work answers go in `--refs`. spec-it never tells the session to keep them: the model refuses any TODO id or issue number in the request (spec_it_models.BANNED), so a request such as 'build todo-k69m, fixes #301' is restated without them, and step 5 (Hand off) hands over only the `next:` line, which `spec_it_api.next_step` builds as `/harness:write-plan "<title>" --spec <path>` with no refs. The two skills therefore agree that ids leave the sheet but neither carries them to the plan; the write-plan session starts from a sheet that, by design, cannot tell it which TODO ids or issues to pass, and the plan's `refs` (and the issue links derived from them) are silently lost.
fix: In spec-it step 5 (and the Rules bullet on implementation notes), state that TODO ids and issue numbers named in the request are kept out of the sheet and appended to the `next:` command as `--refs '<id>' '#<n>'` (quoted, per write-plan step 1), alongside any `-- <guidance>` tail; add a Judgment row for 'the request names a TODO id or issue'.
Have `spec_it.py check` accept an optional `--refs` and print it on the `next:` line, so the driver carries the ids instead of the prose.

important.name: Over-MAX_LINES parse test passes without the line cap
important.summary:
test_parse_refuses_a_page_over_max_lines appends MAX_LINES blank lines to a rendered page and expects ValueError. parse_sheet (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/spec_it_models.py:157-158) also raises ValueError when render_sheet(sheet) != text, and trailing blank lines always fail that round-trip check. Deleting the MAX_LINES guard at spec_it_models.py:144-145 leaves this test green, so the behavior it names (and the SkillSpec node bound to it) has no real guard.

Also (tests): test_the_rendered_page_holds_at_most_max_lines expects a bare ValidationError for 500 goals; it would still pass if a different validator (char cap, duplicate check) fired first after a future change. Likewise test_check_refuses_a_sheet_with_an_id only checks that stderr starts with `problem: `, not that it names the id ("a plan item id").

Also (adv_code_tests): test_parse_refuses_a_page_over_max_lines appends 500 blank lines to a rendered page. That page already fails the render round-trip check at plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/spec_it_models.py:157-158, so the test raises ValueError whether or not the MAX_LINES guard at spec_it_models.py:144-145 exists. No driver test in tests/scripts/test_specsheet_lite.py covers an over-cap page either, so nothing in the suite pins that guard.

Also (adv_code_tests): The MAX_LINES fixture (500 goals) renders 514 lines and the TARGET_LINES driver fixture (250 goals) renders 264 lines. No test renders a page at exactly the cap or target, or one line past it. An off-by-one (> changed to >=) or a cap shifted by up to 13 lines in the model validator at spec_it_models.py:103 or the driver warning at scripts/spec_it.py:54 survives.

Attack: Monkeypatch spec_it_models.MAX_LINES to 10**6, which disables the guard at spec_it_models.py:144-145, then run the test body: parse_sheet(render_sheet(_sheet()) + "\n" * 500) still raises ValueError with 'the page is not in the layout render_sheet writes; rewrite it through the API'. The probe at the run directory's probes/test_probe_tests.py::test_parse_cap_test_passes_with_cap_disabled passed. Deleting lines 144-145 leaves the whole PR suite green.

Attack: Change `if count > MAX_LINES:` at plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/spec_it_models.py:103 to `if count > MAX_LINES + 13:` (or `count > TARGET_LINES + 13` at plugins/harness/scripts/spec_it.py:54): test_the_rendered_page_holds_at_most_max_lines and test_check_warns_past_the_target_length still pass, because their fixtures render 514 and 264 lines (measured by probes/test_probe_tests.py::test_line_counts_of_cap_fixtures).
fix: Pin the refusal reason: `with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="line cap"):`.
Or build a page whose only defect is its length (for example a rendered sheet with over MAX_LINES goal lines written as text, bypassing the model) and assert the cap message.
Add `match="line cap"` to the raises at line 107 and assert `"a plan item id" in done.stderr` in tests/scripts/test_specsheet_lite.py:51.

Build a page that is in render_sheet layout and runs past MAX_LINES (render a sheet via model_construct with enough goals), then assert pytest.raises(ValueError, match="line cap") so only the cap message satisfies it.
Or drop the parse-level guard as redundant with the model validator and rename the test to pin the round-trip refusal it actually exercises.

Size the fixtures from the rendered overhead: compute the base line count of a one-goal sheet, add goals until render_sheet gives exactly MAX_LINES (accepted) and MAX_LINES + 1 (refused). Do the same with TARGET_LINES for the driver warn (no warn at TARGET_LINES, warn at TARGET_LINES + 1).

minor.name: A project override of artifacts.specs or planning_prefixes drops specs from the planning prefixes
minor.summary: docs/SPECS/ joins planning_prefixes only as a literal default. A project that sets artifacts.specs to another folder, or sets its own planning_prefixes list, gets sheets that branch-commit-msg no longer treats as planning documents, with no warning.
fix: In _artifacts, append the specs folder (with a trailing slash) to planning_prefixes when it is missing, and drop the literal from defaults.json; add a config test for an overridden specs value.

minor.name: Slug collapses non-ASCII titles to 'sheet', so distinct same-day sheets collide
minor.summary:
slug keeps only [a-z0-9]; any title written entirely in non-Latin script maps to 'sheet', and titles differing only in punctuation or accents (e.g. 'C++ API' vs 'C# API') map to the same slug. The second write on the same day raises SheetExists for an unrelated sheet, and with replace=True overwrites it.

Attack: Probe (run at PR head): slug('\u8a2d\u8a08') == slug('\u0645\u0631\u062d\u0628\u0627') == 'sheet' and slug('C++ API') == slug('C# API') == 'c-api'. Activate a project, write_sheet(new_sheet('C++ API','R.',['G holds.'], day=D)), then write_sheet(new_sheet('C# API','Other.',['H holds.'], day=D)) raises SheetExists naming the first sheet's file.
fix: Append a short disambiguator when the target exists for a different title (e.g. -2, or a hash of the title), or slug with unicodedata normalization plus a fallback hash for empty results.

minor.name: next_step leaves the --spec path unquoted
minor.summary:
next_step quotes the title but emits '--spec {_rel(path)}' bare (spec_it_api.py:80). artifacts.specs is a free relPath key, and _rel falls back to the absolute path for a sheet outside the project; a folder holding a space (e.g. 'docs/My Specs' or a Windows user folder) yields a next: line whose --spec value splits into two arguments when the developer pastes it.

Also (adv_code_runtime): next_step quotes the title but emits `--spec {_rel(path)}` bare. `spec_it.py check` accepts any path, and artifacts.specs is any relative path, so a sheet under a folder with a space produces a write-plan invocation whose --spec argument is cut at the space.

Attack: With artifacts.specs set to 'docs/my specs', write_sheet(new_sheet('T','R.',['G holds.'], day=date(2026,11,25))) then next_step(sheet, path) returns '/harness:write-plan "T" --spec docs/my specs/2026-11-25-t.md'; write-plan's `--spec PATH` (plugins/harness/skills/write-plan/SKILL.md:4) receives 'docs/my' and a stray positional 'specs/2026-11-25-t.md'.
fix: Quote the path the same way as the title: f'/harness:write-plan "{title}" --spec "{_rel(path)}"', or quote it only when it contains whitespace.
Quote the path in next_step (e.g. `--spec "{_rel(path)}"`) and update the expected string in tests/lib/test_specsheet_lite_api.py:80-81.
Or refuse a path with whitespace in sheet_path/check.

minor.name: Model docstring claims 'no code' but only code fences are refused
minor.summary:
The module docstring says a sheet 'names no plan, skill-spec or TODO id, no issue number, no URL and no code', and the API test docstring repeats it. `BANNED` (lines 27-37) enforces code only as a ``` or ~~~ fence; inline code, function names and file paths pass the model (B7's rationale says so: 'the model bans only fences'). A reader of the docstring would expect the model to reject inline code.

Also (system_shape): The spec_it_models docstring (lines 3-4) says a sheet names 'no code'. SKILL.md:17-18 says the same, and the release note (v1.1.0.md:137) attributes the rule to the model: 'with no ids, issue numbers, URLs or code (`harness_lib.spec_it_models`)'. BANNED (spec_it_models.py:27-37) refuses only ``` and ~~~ fences. Inline code and identifiers in prose pass, and SkillSpec B7 notes that 'the model bans only fences'. Code in prose is the skill's judgment rule (B7), not something the model enforces.
fix: Reword the docstring to 'no code fence' and state that keeping function, field and module names out is the skill's rule, not the model's.
Say 'no code fences' where the model is credited (models docstring, release note), and leave the 'no function or field names' rule to SKILL.md's Outcomes rule, as B7 frames it.

minor.name: A string passed as goals or avoid becomes one goal per character
minor.summary:
The goals/avoid before-validator iterates its value (spec_it_models.py:89-92), and new_sheet calls list(goals) (spec_it_api.py:34). new_sheet(title=..., request=..., goals="Fast") therefore validates into four one-letter goals ['F','a','s','t'] and write_sheet writes them, instead of refusing the wrong type. An agent filling the SKILL.md heredoc with a single string gets a silently malformed sheet that passes check.

Also (adv_code_runtime): SpecSheet._statements (mode='before') iterates `value` directly and new_sheet passes list(goals), so a str argument becomes a list of its characters instead of being refused as a non-list. Depending on the letters, the result is either a silently wrong sheet or a confusing 'appears twice' error.

Attack: Probe (run at PR head): SpecSheet(title='T', request='r', goals='Fast', day=date(2026,11,25)).goals == ['F', 'a', 's', 't']; new_sheet('T', 'R.', 'Fast') writes a sheet with four one-letter goals. new_sheet('T', 'R.', 'Reads the brief') instead raises "the line 'e' appears twice".
fix: In SpecSheet._statements, raise ValueError when value is a str ("goals and avoid are lists of lines") before iterating; optionally make new_sheet pass goals/avoid through unchanged so the model validator sees the original type.
In _statements, raise ValueError when isinstance(value, str) ('goals is a list of lines'); in new_sheet, do the same before list(goals).

minor.name: SKILL.md gives no route to revise an older sheet
minor.summary:
Step 3 says 'Pass replace=True to rewrite a sheet already written from the same title and date', but new_sheet defaults day to today, so revising last week's sheet through the documented heredoc writes a second dated file beside it, and the skill forbids editing the page by hand. load_sheet is exported yet no step uses it.

Also (docs, skill_package, system_shape): SKILL.md step 3 (lines 51-53) says to pass `replace=True` 'to rewrite a sheet already written from the same title and date'. The heredoc it shows never passes `day`, and `new_sheet` dates a sheet today when `day` is None (spec_it_api.py:31-35). Following the step to revise a sheet dated on an earlier day therefore writes a second file under today's date beside the old one, the duplicate the dropped B11 targeted. The skill also never names `load_sheet` or the `day=` argument. Baseline R-16 avoided the duplicate on its own, but the written procedure does not cover the case.

Also (skill_package): spec-it SKILL.md:67 and the Judgment row at line 89 say every refusal names a field to fix. Two refusals do not: `write_sheet` raises `SheetExists` ('<path> exists; pass replace=True to rewrite it') when a sheet with the same title and date exists, and the model-level validator `_whole` refuses a duplicated goal/avoid line or a page over 500 lines without a field. Following the prose literally ('fix that field') gives no action for these.

Also (system_shape): SKILL.md:51-53 says 'Pass replace=True to rewrite a sheet already written from the same title and date'. The heredoc template (lines 56-64) calls new_sheet without `day`, and new_sheet (spec_it_api.py:31-35) defaults to today. An agent that follows the template to revise last week's sheet therefore writes a second file dated today. That is the exact failure B11 targeted, and B11 was dropped only because the baseline happened to pass. load_sheet is already bound in the heredoc namespace, but the skill never shows the revise path.
fix: Add a revise line to Step 3: sheet = load_sheet('<path>'); write_sheet(sheet.model_copy(update={'goals': [...]}), replace=True), which keeps the path and date.

Add a sentence after line 53: 'To revise a sheet, read it with `load_sheet(<path>)` and pass its `day` to `new_sheet` (`day=old.day`) with `replace=True`, so the page keeps its path and date.' Add the matching row to the Judgment table.

Reword line 67 to: 'A refusal is one `problem:` line naming what to fix (a field, a repeated line, the page length, or an existing sheet, which `replace=True` rewrites): fix it and run the heredoc again.' and align the Judgment row at line 89.

Add a revise line under step 3, for example: 'To revise a sheet, load it and rewrite it in place: `sheet = load_sheet("<path>").model_copy(update={"goals": [...]})` then `write_sheet(sheet, replace=True)`; the title and date stay, so the path does not change.' SKILL.md is a frozen part, so this goes through reopen and refreeze.

minor.name: Absolute-path refusal test accepts any exception
minor.summary:
test_specs_refuses_an_absolute_path uses `pytest.raises(Exception)`, so a KeyError, a TypeError or a make_project failure would all pass it. The refusal comes from schema validation as ConfigError (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/config.py:344-347, relPath at harness.schema.json:52).

Also (overall): `test_specs_refuses_an_absolute_path` uses `pytest.raises(Exception)`, so it also passes when load_config breaks for an unrelated reason (a KeyError from a missing default, a TypeError in `_artifacts`). load_config reports schema violations as `ConfigError` (config.py:25, 347).

Also (roast): test_specs_refuses_an_absolute_path wraps load_config in pytest.raises(Exception), so a KeyError from a missing specs key in the builder or a fixture failure would also pass it.
fix: Import ConfigError and assert `with pytest.raises(ConfigError, match="specs"):`, building the project outside the raises block.
Import `ConfigError` from harness_lib.config and use `pytest.raises(ConfigError, match='specs')`.

minor.name: Default-date test races midnight
minor.summary:
test_new_sheet_dates_today_by_default calls date.today() inside new_sheet and again in the assertion. A run that crosses midnight between the two calls fails even though the code is correct.

Attack: Patch harness_lib.spec_it_api.date with a stub whose today() returns 2026-11-25 on the first call and 2026-11-26 on the second (which is what a run straddling midnight sees): the assertion sheet.day == date.today() fails.
fix: Bracket the call: before = date.today(); sheet = new_sheet(...); assert before <= sheet.day <= date.today().

minor.name: Goal, avoid and title lines with Unicode line breaks validate and write but never load back
minor.summary:
_statement refuses only '\n' and '\r', and the title validator only '\n', while render_sheet/parse_sheet split the page with str.splitlines(), which also breaks on \x0b, \x0c, \x1c-\x1e, \x85, \u2028 and \u2029. A SpecSheet holding one of these constructs, write_sheet writes it, and load_sheet / `spec_it.py check` then refuse the page the API itself wrote, breaking the stated contract that render_sheet's page is the whole stored form parse_sheet reads back.

Attack: Probe (run at PR head): SpecSheet(title='T', request='r', goals=['one\u2028two'], day=date(2026,11,25)) constructs fine; parse_sheet(render_sheet(sheet)) raises "Goals holds a line that is not a '- ' item: 'two'". Same for goals=['one\x0ctwo'] and ['one\x85two'], and title='T\rX' fails with 'the page is not in the layout render_sheet writes'. Through the API: activate a project, write_sheet(new_sheet('T','r',['one\u2028two'])) returns a path, then load_sheet(path) raises ValueError and `spec_it.py check <that path>` exits 1.
fix: In _statement and SpecSheet._title, refuse any text where text.splitlines() != [text] (covers every separator splitlines honors, including '\r' for the title).
Alternatively normalize those characters to a space in _clean before validation.

This file becomes the GitHub release body, so it would publish a stale state.

The head contradicts it: SkillSpec.json records B10's baseline R-9 and greens R-10/R-15, freeze r2.5 closed round 2, and r3.2 froze round 3 with B11-B13 dropped (their baselines R-16..R-18 did not fail). The head carries the r2.5 and r3.2 freezes, B10 green and B11-B13 dropped; the entry mentions neither the third round nor the dropped behaviors, and this file becomes the GitHub release body.
